chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام), ‘May I be sacrificed for you, by what is the Imam recognized?’ He said: ‘By qualities. As for the first of them, it is that there has preceded from his father concerning him an indication toward him, so that it may be a proof against them. He is asked and he answers; and if one remains silent from asking him, he initiates; and he informs of what will be tomorrow; and he speaks to the people in every tongue.’

Then he said to me, ‘O Abu Muhammad, I shall give you a sign before you rise.’ It was not long before a man from the people of Khurasan entered upon us. The Khurasani spoke to him in Arabic, and Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام) answered him in Persian. So the Khurasani said to him, ‘By Allah, may I be sacrificed for you, nothing prevented me from speaking to you in Khurasani except that I thought you did not know it well.’ He said, ‘Glory be to Allah! If I were not able to answer you, then what excellence would I have over you?’

Then he said to me, ‘O Abu Muhammad, the Imam is not unaware of the speech of any among the people, nor of a bird, nor of a beast, nor of anything in which there is a spirit. So whoever does not possess these qualities is not an Imam.’

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The divinely appointed Imam, recognized through specific signs and qualities.
key_terms.بِإِشَارَةٍ: By explicit indication from the previous Imam toward his successor.
key_terms.بِخِصَالٍ: By distinct characteristics or qualities that identify the true Imam.
key_terms.بِكُلِّ لِسَانٍ: In every language, indicating universal communicative knowledge.
key_terms.حُجَّةً: A binding proof against the people, leaving no excuse after clarification.
key_terms.عَلَامَةً: A sign given as demonstrative evidence of the Imam’s status.
key_terms.فَضْلِي: My excellence or merit, referring to the distinguishing superiority of the Imam.
key_terms.لَا يَخْفَى عَلَيْهِ: Nothing is hidden from him, referring here to speech and communication.

ai.seo_question: How is the Imam recognized according to this hadith from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the Imam is recognized through divinely granted signs, including explicit designation by the preceding Imam, immediate and authoritative knowledge, foreknowledge by Allah’s permission, and the ability to speak with people in every language. It presents these qualities as proofs of the Imam’s divine authority and as distinguishing marks that set the true Imam apart from others.
